items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1958-09-24
items.q: The trombone player sitting next to me was Caesar Petrello, Jimmy Petrello's brother.

ctx.x: And did your father play ragtime?

Well, in them days there was what you call, it wasn't ragtime in them days. My father did. You know, it was dance fans, you know, but there wasn't no pep, you know? It was a regular, legitimate resistance, you see? Of course, they played with what was called ragtime in them days, but none of them was out there the Negroes. You see, my daddy gave it up. My daddy gave up music out when I was about ten years old, you see? You know, I'll never forget I was a young kid. First time I stood out all night, played with a…
I'm not going to be a man. I'm not going to be a man. I'm not going to be a man. I'm not going to be a man.
